title: A Wet Quarter
text: A 1987 quarter the Drenched Man paid with. It never dries. It smells like the reservoir — algae, rust, and something sweeter underneath.

title: The Reflection That Stayed
text: CAM 2, 11:58 PM. The college student walks away from the machine. Her reflection in the glass stays for another forty seconds, looking at you.

title: The Dog on Camera
text: CAM 1, 2:21 AM. The girl with the empty leash. On camera, there is a small dog at the end of it, wagging. In person, there is nothing.

title: Receipt: Welcome Back
text:
Printed at 5:41 AM with no sale.
MERIDIAN ROADSIDE SERVICES — UNIT 313
THANK YOU FOR YOUR SERVICE, NO. 0
WELCOME BACK.

title: Ticket: Coach 313
text:
The Passenger's ticket.
MERIDIAN COACH LINES — COACH 313
KESSLER FLATS → HOLLOWAY TERMINAL
DATE: 10/13/87   DEP: 2:58 AM
The paper is soft, as if it has been underwater for a very long time.

title: Drawing: The Bus
text: A crayon drawing pressed against the glass by the Silent Child. A yellow bus with the number 313, upside down in blue scribbles. A woman stands on the shore. Her mouth is drawn far too wide.

title: Note in the Can
text:
Folded inside the unlabeled can, dry despite everything:

'If you're reading this, the machine likes you. Don't let it like you too much. Don't sell him anything it makes. — M.'

title: The Unstamped Revision
text: A handbook page that appeared on its own during Night 3. It carries a purple 'REV. 3:13' stamp instead of the green District Office seal. Rule A5 says unsealed pages are not policy.

title: Walter's Confession
text: The real Walter, Night 3: 'They pulled my bus out of the water and they didn't scrap it. They built that machine out of it. That's why we come here. It's the last stop.'

title: Drawing: Someone Inside
text: The child's second drawing: the vending machine, drawn carefully, row by row. Behind the glass, between the cans, a woman's face. She has a name tag. It says 0.

title: CAM 0
text: A camera feed that was never on your monitor before. Label: OBSERVATION — DISTRICT. It shows the booth from behind. It shows you.

title: Photograph: Adeline Marsh
text: A water-stained photo the child pressed to the glass. A tired woman with a soft, crooked smile holds a little girl in a yellow raincoat. Written on the back: 'Addie & Lily, Sept. 1987.' This is not the face of the woman who keeps asking about her daughter.

title: Small Brass Key
text: The child slid it under the glass. Stamped on the bow: STOCKROOM LOCKER 0.

title: Employee File: M. Quill
text:
MERIDIAN ROADSIDE SERVICES — PERSONNEL
Name: Mara Quill. Position: Night Attendant, Unit 313.
Badge: 0412 — struck out by hand. Written over it: 'No. 0'.
Status: TRANSFERRED (INTERNAL).
Notes: 'Exceptional retention. Bonded well with unit.'

title: Tape: M.Q. #1
text:
[Cassette, stockroom recorder]
MARA: 'Night forty. The customers after 3:13 aren't customers. They're passengers. Thirteen of them, from the bus. The machine keeps them here, and every time we sell them something, a little of what's left of them goes into the coin box. Hale calls it change.'
[Knocking on the tape. Close.]
MARA: 'He's here. I'm keeping the panel shut.'

title: Maintenance Log, Unit 313
text:
MAINTENANCE — UNIT 313 (rebuilt from salvage, 1988)
— Row E dispensed unrequested item: 47 occurrences. Do not log further.
— Coin box emptied by District. Contents: 'non-currency.'
— Override keypad installed per contract clause 13. Code held by District.
— Knocking from inside unit: normal. Do not open.

title: Mara's Shift Notes
text:
Torn pages in Mara's handwriting:
'The override doesn't free the machine by itself. It needs the date, every name, and nobody left behind.'
'THE DATE IS MONTH AND DAY. NOT THE TIME. He wants you to try the time.'
'Manifest — behind the loose panel under the shelf. Hale doesn't know I found it.'

title: Newspaper Clipping
text:
KESSLER COUNTY LEDGER — October 14, 1987
BUS PLUNGES INTO RESERVOIR; 13 FEARED DEAD
A Meridian Coach Lines bus left Route 9 near Kessler Flats at approximately 3:13 a.m. Tuesday, October 13, breaking through the guard rail into Kessler Reservoir. Driver Walter Pruitt, 58, was among those missing. A witness reported the driver swerved to avoid 'a tall figure in the road.'

title: Passenger Manifest, Coach 313
text:
MERIDIAN COACH LINES — MANIFEST — COACH 313 — 10/13/87
Driver: Walter Pruitt
1. Ellis Crane  2. Adeline Marsh  3. Lily Marsh (7)  4. Tomas Reyes  5. June Albright  6. Harold & 7. Ruth Bell  8. Samuel Okonkwo  9. Della Ferris  10. Ivan Petrov  11. Grace Lin  12. Marcus Webb
At the bottom, in green ink: 'Every name. Say them if you have to. — M.'

title: Drawing: Thirteen
text: The child's third drawing: the reservoir at night, thirteen stick figures in a line, holding hands. Above them, in careful numbers: 10 13. One of the figures is very small and wearing yellow.

title: Badge No. 0
text: Mara left her badge on the counter. The plastic is fogged from the inside. The number has been scratched away and replaced with 0. On the back: 'Whoever's next — I'm sorry. I almost had it.'

title: Tape: M.Q. #2
text:
[Cassette, dispensed from Row E]
MARA: 'The 3:13 isn't the time it crashed. It's the time it stopped. The Collector stood in the road and the bus went in, and he's kept that one minute open ever since. Every night it opens, they come back to the last stop, and Meridian sells them things until there's nothing left to sell. The company gets its luck. He gets the change. And the machine gets someone to run it forever.'

title: How to Break the Contract
text: Mara, Night 6: 'Three things. The date — month and day, on the maintenance keypad, while he's standing in front of you. Every name — the manifest. And nobody left behind: Walter has to be ready to go, Mr. Crane has to know where he's going, and Lily has to be safe from that thing wearing her mother.'

title: Hospital Record
text:
KESSLER COUNTY GENERAL — 10/13/87 — Admissions log, photocopied by Nurse Okafor.
'03:40 — Female, approx. 35, recovered from reservoir shoreline. Unresponsive. Persistent rictus (smile). Expired 04:02. No ID. Body not claimed. Body not located at morning count.'

title: A Glimpse of the Ledger
text: For a second, the Collector's ledger fell open. Columns of names. Beside each one, a row of tiny coins. The last line is blank, except for a column heading: ATTENDANT.
